content: Composite/multi-factor stock scoring: equal weighting of factors (value, growth, momentum, quality) is a common simple baseline that is 'very difficult to beat out-of-sample' despite being naive, per factor-investing literature (Alpha Architect, Deutsche Bank 'Seven Sins of Quant Investing'). But equal-weighting has known failure modes: value and momentum are often negatively correlated so equal-weight can cancel signal in either direction rather than surface consensus; linear/z-score combination is sensitive to outliers and requires normalization; dynamically-weighted factors can beat equal-weight but require regime-timing skill retail users don't have and risk overfitting. Practical takeaway for a personal tool: rank-based (percentile) scoring instead of raw z-scores reduces outlier sensitivity; show the sub-scores alongside the composite (don't hide the components) so equal-weight blending is inspectable, not a black box.
